claims.text: This package may read, prompt, record and verify. It has no writing, editing, applying or promotion capability anywhere, by construction rather than by promise
claims.why: The chunk only re-exports functions from bus.py; it does not contain the implementation of any capability. Whether the package has writing/editing/applying/promotion capabilities cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: A council's product is a queue of CHECKS for the existing deterministic gate (tests, fences, diffs) to run; the gate's result is the only verdict.
claims.why: This claim is about the behavior of the package as a whole; this chunk only re-exports transcript functions. No code here produces checks or interacts with a gate.

claims.text: Dissent is recorded verbatim and is never averaged away, which is why nothing in this package carries an approve / reject / score / majority / consensus / confidence field.
claims.why: The chunk does not define any data structures; it only re-exports names. The absence of such fields across the entire package cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Advisory-by-docstring is not a control; ABSENCE OF THE FIELD is the control.
claims.why: This is a design principle, not a checkable behavior. The chunk does not contain the fields or the control logic.

claims.text: The premise -- independent vendors have independent blind spots -- is plausible and UNTESTED. It is measured before session.py is wired into any real review workflow, and the module is deleted if it fails.
claims.why: This refers to future or external wiring (session.py) and to deletion of the module; none of that is observable in this chunk.

claims.text: ARM A: four vendors (anthropic / openai / google / local), one round each.
claims.why: This is a protocol description; no code in this chunk implements the experiment.

claims.text: CONTROL: ONE vendor asked twice under two different role prompts. If four vendors do not beat one-vendor-twice, the council has bought four egress paths, an ssh surface and 4x latency for a prompt-diversity effect.
claims.why: This is a protocol description; no code in this chunk implements the experiment.

claims.text: GROUND TRUTH: spine.attempt.GateResult.passed and AttemptResult.state -- already recorded, free to harvest.
claims.why: The chunk does not reference spine.attempt or any GateResult/AttemptResult; these are external to this chunk.

claims.text: INDEPENDENCE: pairwise agreement rate BETWEEN vendors versus WITHIN one vendor across two calls.
claims.why: This is a protocol description; no code in this chunk implements the measurement.

claims.text: FALSIFIER: if inter-vendor agreement is within noise of intra-vendor agreement on N patches, THIS MODULE IS DELETED.
claims.why: This is a protocol description; no code in this chunk implements the falsifier or deletion.

claims.text: SMALL-N CAVEAT, stated in advance: the independent corpus is ~17-20 tasks. That is not enough for a significance claim. The honest move is to say so now rather than to report a percentage afterwards.
claims.why: This is a caveat about a corpus; no code or data in this chunk supports or contradicts it.

observations.what: The package docstring makes many strong behavioral claims, but this chunk only re-exports from bus.py; the actual enforcement is elsewhere.

The docstring promises the package has no writing/editing/applying/promotion capability, but the re-exported functions (append_roster, append_round, append_turn) sound like they write to a transcript.
The docstring says the council store is at runs/council/<council_id>.jsonl, but the function council_store_path is not defined here; its implementation in bus.py determines the actual path.
